speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) what is Singapore’s position on the recent unsuccessful draft UN Security Council resolution to recommend granting the State of Palestine full membership in the United Nations; and (b) what are Singapore's considerations to support such a recommendation, in light of Singapore's voting record of abstention on the status of Palestine in the United Nations as a non-Member Observer State at the 67th UN General Assembly on 29 November 2012.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) whether Singapore will consider establishing full diplomatic relations with the State of Palestine; and (b) if not, what are Singapore's considerations for not doing so.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have consistently advocated for a negotiated two-state solution that is consistent with the relevant United Nations (UN) Security Council resolutions because we believe this is a way for Israelis and Palestinians to live side by side in peace and security.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, this is the only viable path for achieving a comprehensive, a just and a durable solution to this conflict.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have also consistently supported the right of the Palestinian people to a homeland.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In 1988, the Palestinian Liberation Organisation (PLO) issued a proclamation on the State of Palestine which affirmed the UN's partition of the Mandate of Palestine into an Arab and a Jewish State, as well as the PLO's decision to renounce violence against Israel.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We welcomed this proclamation back in 1988 because the PLO had therefore explicitly rejected terrorism and recognised the right of the State of Israel to exist.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We saw these moves as progress towards a durable solution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On 10 May 2024, the General Assembly took up a resolution expressing support for Palestine's membership in the UN and recommended that the Security Council reconsider this matter favourably.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore voted in favour of this resolution after very careful consideration.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This reflected our hope to encourage both Israel and Palestine to resume direct negotiations towards a two-state solution, at a time when, in fact, the prospects for such negotiations were increasingly bleak.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We therefore decided to join the majority of the international community in supporting this resolution, which is also in line with our long-standing support for the principles of international law and for the implementation of all relevant UN Security Council resolutions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will make this move at an appropriate time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our key consideration is that such a move on our part should help progress towards peace and a negotiated two-state solution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In particular, there will need to be an effective Palestinian government that accepts Israel's right to exist and categorically rejects terrorism.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Both sides have legitimate rights and both peoples have a right to live in peace and dignity within secure borders.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We urge both sides to seize the moment, to take steps towards a long-lasting peace and to put an end to the suffering that has gone on for far too long.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Ultimately, Israelis and Palestinians need to exercise leadership and will have to work together to forge a better future for their peoples.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As Singapore is a friend to both, Singapore will continue to offer our encouragement and our tangible support to both Palestinians and Israelis.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: To date, we have trained more than 750 officials in a variety of areas, including diplomacy, water management, economic development and urban planning.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: These are important vital areas that any government will need have the necessary expertise in.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: During my recent visit to Ramallah in March 2024, the Prime Minister of Palestine, Mohammad Mustafa expressed his appreciation for our long-standing technical assistance and, in fact, he sought further capacity-building support, especially in civil service training and in digitalisation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I welcomed his interest in these areas and I said that Singapore will do our best to respond.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As a follow-up, there will be a course on "Transforming Public Service with the Power of Artificial Intelligence" which we will conduct for Palestinian Authority officials later this month.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will also provide fully funded scholarships for Palestinian officials to pursue postgraduate studies in our local universities.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Three Palestinian officials have already been awarded scholarships this year, I think in accountancy, international political economy and info-communications security.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We hope that this training opportunities will help the Palestinian Authority officials better serve the Palestinian people, as well as equip them with necessary skills when it comes to the eventual reconstruction of Gaza.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On Mr Faisal Manap's specific question on training Palestinian officials to aid in the reconstruction of Gaza, let me just state that Singapore will assess how best we can help bilaterally and, in fact, as part of a multilateral effort.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I remain in close and constant contact with all my counterparts in the Middle East on this issue.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore participated in a conference co-hosted by King Abdullah II of Jordan, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah Al Sisi and the UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on 11 June this year to discuss the humanitarian response to Gaza.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We stand ready to contribute, taking into account Gaza's needs and in account of our own resources and expertise.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But clearly, all these can only take effect when the fighting ceases.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For now, the focus has to be on securing an immediate humanitarian ceasefire in Gaza and the release of all the hostages immediately.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Specifically, would it happen only when a two-state solution is negotiated and concluded?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If so, this is no different from Singapore's previous position.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Lastly, would the Minister agree that the recognition of Palestine would allow for negotiations to proceed on a more equal footing between two recognised states, the State of Israel and the State of Palestine, rather than one state negotiating with a non-state entity?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, I thank him for accompanying me on my trip to the Middle East in March.

But a key point and the prickly question which every single country that is pondering this question has to decide is: is there an effective Palestine government or leadership who represents all Palestinians which has effective control over, at the minimum, the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, and has the mandate, has the authority to negotiate with the Israelis on behalf of the Palestinians?

And, quite frankly, I think every other country in the world will have to grapple with this same question but will arrive at that answer, probably at a different threshold or a different point in time.
Frankly, it will also depend on their own domestic circumstances.
Within those parameters, I look forward to progress.
I do not know exactly when that will happen, but I certainly look forward to progress.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Speaker, I thank the hon Minister for the response to my question.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Under international law, there are conditions for the recognition of a statehood.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, has the Ministry conferred with the Attorney-General and Ministry of Law to assess whether Singapore would be ready to recognise a particular state and whether that state fulfils those conditions of being recognised as a state under international law, because it has repercussions on international treaties and other enforcement of court orders?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The second supplementary question is: with the Minister, we visited our officers in the Ramallah Representative Office and met participants from the ETAP batches and they are all very thankful for the Singapore Government's support.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My question is: if Singapore recognises the Palestinian state right now, what kind of further support to the Palestinian Authority could Singapore provide which we have not already provided or are unable to provide right now?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Likewise, I thank the Member Mr Zhulkarnain for accompanying me.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: He was in Ramallah with me and when we had the discussions with the Palestinian Authority leadership, including their graduates of our ETAP programme.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We intend to continue all our assistance packages.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We intend to also look for opportunities to do more.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And quite frankly, the level of support that we provide to the Palestinian Authority will not depend upon whether or not there is formal recognition or not or, indeed, what happens even on the international stage.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Member will know, in fact, all Members will know, even without that formal status, the Palestinian Prime Minister has visited Singapore, our then Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong has been to Ramallah, Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean and I and Second Minister Maliki have made numerous trips to Ramallah.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, the point I want to assure Members is that the interactions, the support and the assistance that we provide to the Palestinian Authority are not subject to the other political and diplomatic interactions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Actually, the formal recognition of statehood is not just a diplomatic or just a legal question.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: More specifically, in the case of Palestine as the situation currently subsists, you can make legal arguments both ways whether or not they fulfil the four criteria of the Montevideo Principles of Statehood.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Permanent people define boundaries, effective government able to transact, enter treaties.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Ultimately, we believe this is a political question and, therefore, it will be subject to the political considerations of the different entities that are trying to engage the Palestinian people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We believe that the Palestinian people have a right to a homeland.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will continue to support the Palestinian people and the nascent Palestinian Authority, which, certainly, in the case of the PLO, constitutes, I would say, the key pillar of the current Palestinian Authority, which accepts Israel's right to exist and which has renounced terrorism.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Member was there in the room when I had these discussions with numerous Palestinian Authority leaders who all reaffirmed these points.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we really have no problem with the Palestinian Authority.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I think let us be frank about it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The situation in Gaza is far more problematical and the people whom we spoke to and engaged in Ramallah have tenuous or, in fact, almost zero input into the situation in Gaza.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Nevertheless, let us be helpful, constructive and consistent.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Let us engage in constructive, direct assistance to the people of Palestine who need and, as the Member has noticed, appreciate our support.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: First question: what is our total official aid given to the Palestinians over the last 10 years?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Second question, which is also one of my questions for written answer actually, is whether our country has made any defence sales, such as weapons or any other material that can cause harm to civilians, to Israel since 7 October 2023?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do not have the total aid provided to Palestine over the past 10 years.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I said in my earlier answer, we obviously have the $10 million enhanced technical assistance package, we have scholarships.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I am giving the Member figures which frankly are all within less than one calendar year.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If the Member really wants the total for 10 years, he can submit a separate question later on.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Apart from this, it is the established policy of the Government not to publicly divulge any details of defence sales for national security reasons.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Can the Minister share more on any diplomatic efforts that we are currently taking with international and regional bodies, like the UN, where a vote has been taken in favour of Palestinian membership; the European Union, where 10 out of 27 states now formally recognise Palestine and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), our closest neighbours to facilitate the realisation of the Palestinian state, a two-state solution, and to secure the legal and diplomatic rights of Palestine after this conflict is over?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are approaching the end of Question Time.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I request the Minister to address that and I see a few more hands.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, let us keep all the answers and questions short.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are trying our best bilaterally on the basis of our relationship with Israel, our relationship with all the Middle East stakeholders, as well as consulting closely with our ASEAN partners and other partners around the world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I just want to emphasise again: we are not the determinative factor.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I honestly do not know how and when it will end, and my focus is not to add fuel to the fire, but to be quietly, discreetly, constructively helpful to the people at a humanitarian level and to build up capacity, specifically with respect to the Palestinian Authority.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: In response to the Minister's answer to my supplementary question just now, I think we are dealing with a Catch-22 situation here.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Most people will agree that an effective Palestinian government that governs the entire territory is still in the works.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: However, we are waiting for a viable and effective Palestinian state to exist before recognising it.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: The Minister said that one key principle guiding our actions is whether it can bring forward the peace process.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Therefore, does the Minister agree that Singapore's recognition of Palestine will help, even in some small way, to bring forward the peace process and negotiations, or will it hurt the process?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I know Mr Giam is sincere in this, but I would point out that even in his question, there are two different dimensions to it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: One, is there an effective Palestinian leadership that speaks for all and that has the mandate to negotiate?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And there will be peroxisomes of wars, conflicts and horrendous humanitarian disasters which we are witnessing now.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I hope I have explained to everyone here, including the people, the principled position and the motivation behind our position.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is why we do not engage in polemic or in performative gestures, or making premature pronouncements – which frankly, would be unhelpful – and also, be humble enough to know, Singapore is a tiny city state far away.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Member has been there, so he knows the difficulty and complexities of the conflict.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, another worthwhile reminder for all of us in Singapore: this is fundamentally not our quarrel.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is a family quarrel in another family.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The worst thing you can do in a family quarrel is to get involved unnecessarily or with ulterior motives, or to perform for an external audience.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, let us remain calm, let us remain united, let us remain constructive and helpful, and hope even in this time of bleak, darkness, hope that peace will be given a chance in Palestine and that our Israeli friends and our Palestinian friends – brothers actually, the two of them – can live in peace with each other.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For Members who have accompanied me on my trips, I hope you have noticed that we actually have an unusual and unique privilege that we are welcomed by all sides.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you think about that, that is not something that you can take for granted.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It does not mean agreeing with everyone all the time, but even when we disagree with elements of other people's programmes, other people's agenda, they understand why we disagree and they know that we mean well and that we are good for our word and that we are helpful.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, that is the attitude by which the Government of Singapore approaches this most vexing of disputes, which has gone on for far too long.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister of State Sun Xueling, we are actually at the end of Question Time, but you wish to add something?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
